questions.stem: ___ the client complained about was the lack of communication.

why_wrong: B : « Which » ne convient pas ici.
C : « It » appelle « It was … that ».
D : « That » ne peut pas ouvrir une phrase clivée en « What… was ».
B: 'Which' does not fit here.
C: 'It' calls for 'It was … that'.
D: 'That' cannot open a 'What… was' cleft.

questions.stem: It was Ms. Hoffman ___ proposed the new pricing strategy.

why_wrong: A : « which » n'est pas pour une personne.
B : « whom » est un complément ; ici c'est le sujet.
C : « what » ne convient pas dans « It was… that/who ».
A: 'which' is not for people.
B: 'whom' is an object; here it is the subject.
C: 'what' does not fit 'It was… that/who'.

questions.stem: What matters most ___ the quality of the service, not the price.

why_wrong: A : Temps et accord incohérents.
C : « What matters » est suivi de « is » (singulier).
D : Participe sans auxiliaire : phrase incomplète.
A: Inconsistent tense and agreement.
C: 'What matters' takes 'is' (singular).
D: Participle with no auxiliary: incomplete sentence.

questions.stem: It was in 2018 ___ the company opened its first overseas office.

why_wrong: A : « which » exigerait un antécédent chose.
B : « who » est réservé aux personnes.
D : « what » ne convient pas ici.
fr.example: It was last week that we met.

why_wrong: A: 'which' would need a thing antecedent.
B: 'who' is for people.
D: 'what' does not fit here.
en.example: It was last week that we met.

questions.stem: Which sentence emphasizes the reason for the delay?
choices: It the storm was that caused the delay.
The storm caused the delay that.
What the storm was caused the delay.
It was the storm that caused the delay.

why_wrong: A : Ordre incorrect.
B : Ordre incorrect.
C : Structure impossible.
fr.example: It was the noise that annoyed me.

why_wrong: A: Wrong order.
B: Wrong order.
C: Impossible structure.
en.example: It was the noise that annoyed me.

questions.stem: All ___ we need now is your signature.

why_wrong: A : « which » ne s'emploie pas après « all ».
C : « who » est pour une personne.
D : Après « all », on emploie « that » (ou rien).
fr.example: All that remains is to sign.

why_wrong: A: 'which' is not used after 'all'.
C: 'who' is for people.
D: After 'all', use 'that' (or nothing).
en.example: All that remains is to sign.

questions.stem: I really ___ appreciate your quick response.

why_wrong: A : Sujet « I » : « do ».
B : Le contexte est au présent.
C : « am appreciate » est impossible.
A: Subject 'I': 'do'.
B: The context is present.
C: 'am appreciate' is impossible.

questions.stem: The reason ___ we cancelled the event was the weather.

why_wrong: B : « what » ne convient pas après « reason ».
C : « reason for » exigerait un nom ensuite.
D : « reason » est suivi de « why ».
fr.example: The reason why he left is clear.

why_wrong: B: 'what' does not fit after 'reason'.
C: 'reason for' would need a noun after it.
D: 'reason' is followed by 'why'.
en.example: The reason why he left is clear.
